issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking specific performance of a contract for sale of immovable property, without specifically claiming possession or seeking direct adjudication of title, is not a suit for land.
material_facts: The agreement concerned the sale of land and a building situated outside the territorial limits of the High Court’s ordinary original jurisdiction.
The plaintiffs sought a declaration that the sale agreement and memorandum remained binding and a decree for specific performance.
The agreement provided for possession to be handed over upon execution of the sale deed, but the plaint did not specifically claim delivery of possession.
The plaintiffs obtained leave to sue, and the defendant sought to have that leave revoked on the ground that the suit was a suit for land.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not a suit for land under clause 12 of the Letters Patent. The order refusing to revoke leave was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a suit is a suit for land is determined from the plaint and the reliefs claimed. A suit is for land when the relief relates to adjudication of title to, or delivery of possession of, the land. Under section 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, possession in addition to specific performance must be specifically claimed before it may be granted. The Court agreed with the approach of Mahajan J. in M/s Moolji Jaitha and Co. v. The Khandesh Spinning and Weaving Mills Co. Ltd.; it also referred to Velliappa Chettiar v. Govinda Doss and Debendra Nath Chowdhury v. Southern Bank Ltd.

predicates.specific_performance_case: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking enforcement of a contract to transfer immovable property.
predicates.no_possession_relief_claimed: The plaintiff did not specifically ask the court to order delivery of possession of the property.
predicates.no_direct_title_adjudication_sought: The plaintiff did not ask the court to directly adjudicate competing claims to title to the property.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks specific performance of a property-transfer contract without specifically claiming possession or asking for direct adjudication of title, the suit is not a suit for land.
